q: When writing a page for the letterpress compiler, who writes the HTML and CSS — the model or the compiler — and what evidence supports that split?
note: The model emits ops only. The direct-HTML control arms failed every render gate; the failures were numeric constraints a model cannot evaluate.

q: In letterpress ops, how do you set two or three words of a title in the accent colour?
note: Square brackets inside text= itself. There is no mark= argument.

q: How many colours does a letterpress THEME line name, and what produces the rest of the palette?
note: Exactly one 6-digit accent hex; the compiler derives ten tokens, each solved against its own background for contrast.

q: Write a letterpress TEXT op that gives section s1 an eyebrow reading Weekly loaf. Which key holds the slot name and which holds the words?
note: TEXT sec=s1 slot=eyebrow text="Weekly loaf" — the slot is the value of slot=, the words go in text=.

q: The brief for a bakery states no numbers at all. What should a letterpress proof section contain?
note: Emit nothing. Asked for a stats band on a numberless brief a 4B invented 140ms, $3.8k/yr and 99% accuracy.

q: In a letterpress proof section, what goes in an ITEM's title= and what goes in its body=?
note: title= is the figure exactly as the brief writes it; body= is one short line saying what it counts.

q: Can a model driving letterpress write a customer quote attributed to a named person, and why or why not?
note: Never. There is no computable ground truth for a testimonial — the brief has no customers, so every possible answer is fabricated.

q: A letterpress FAQ answer contains an opening time the brief never stated. What happens to that line before it reaches the page?
note: Neither may be stated. A reader acts on price and clock time; any line containing an unstated one is deleted.

q: Which letterpress motif suits a sourdough bakery, and which one must not be used just because it is first in the list?
note: lattice is the over-under weave for craft and material. elevation is a building and belongs to premises only.

q: A film archive holds regional television from 1957 to 1994. Which letterpress motif is drawn for a subject defined by the years it covers?
note: strata — stacked bands cut by a section line, for a span of time.

q: Which letterpress motif belongs to a command-line tool that scans Postgres databases?
note: schematic — nodes on a grid joined by routed runs, for software and infrastructure.

q: Who writes the text shown under a letterpress figure, and does MEDIA accept an alt= argument?
note: MEDIA takes slot= and motif= only. The compiler drew the picture and captions it; models caption drawings as though they were photographs.

q: A letterpress page has a hero figure and a detail figure. What rule governs the two motifs?
note: They must differ. Ten of twelve generated pages once used the same drawing twice.

q: How long should the body of a letterpress features ITEM be, and what should the second part contain?
note: Two sentences: what it is, then one concrete detail — a duration, a material, a step, a limit.

q: What must a letterpress cta title avoid, and what should it say instead?
note: It must not restate the hero headline; say the next thing — when to come, what happens first, what it costs.

q: Which sections does a letterpress page always open and close with, and how many go between them?
note: Opens hero, closes cta, three or four chosen for the business between them.

q: Why must a letterpress page plan include a detail section or another section carrying a drawing?
note: Otherwise the page is an unbroken column of prose — features, faq and roster are all text.

q: A letterpress faq answer needs specifics to feel concrete. Where must those specifics come from?
note: Everything in an answer must come from the brief; faq is where invented facts appear most freely.

q: Which letterpress features layout is preferred, list or grid, and what is wrong with the other?
note: list renders numerals on hairline rules; grid renders bordered cards, which read as a component library.

q: What goes in the title= of a letterpress roster ITEM, and what must never go there?
note: A role or a service. Never a person's name — the same refusal as the testimonial rule.

q: What happens to a six-section letterpress page where every section uses tone=quiet?
note: It reads as one continuous column however different the sections are. Alternate quiet, bold and inverted.

q: When the letterpress compiler substitutes a default for something invalid, what does it do about it, and why does that matter for measurement?
note: Every substitution is reported. A generous compiler produces a handsome page from a failed generation and you would read the compiler's work as the model's.

q: What does the letterpress compiler do with slot=item inside a hero section?
note: Rejected, never coerced. Slots are legal per kind.

q: What does a letterpress note section contain, and how many should a page have?
note: A title and a lede, nothing else — no eyebrow, button or drawing. At most one per page.
